basis: May 31, 2023 is the earliest qualifying disclosure I could verify. Nordstrom reported consolidated GAAP revenue of $3,181 million for fiscal Q1 2023 versus $3,569 million a year earlier, a 10.87% decline and below the $3,390.55 million cutoff. The two reviews agree on that result. The earliest date remains open because I located the separate 23-page March 2 earnings deck but could not read its substantive slide content. The complete call transcript resolves the spoken guidance: the revenue forecast covered the first half, and the Q1 breakeven forecast concerned EBIT. Neither establishes a numeric Q1 revenue ceiling.

coverage.detail: November 22, 2022, preceding earnings cycle. The Q3 release maintained a 5%–7% revenue growth outlook for fiscal 2022, which ended January 28, 2023.

Recovered the November 22 call transcript on Nordstrom’s press site. Management discussed softer demand, Q4 and inventory entering 2023. The call supplied no numeric fiscal Q1 2023 revenue ceiling. The separate Q3 slide file at https://investor.nordstrom.com/static-files/06f25a76-8695-4ac6-92b5-4b64ea7188d0 and its press.nordstrom.com counterpart both returned 403.

December 6 Morgan Stanley Global Consumer and Retail Conference. Nordstrom’s 11-page transcript identifies the CEO, interim CFO and Morgan Stanley moderator. The holiday-volume and inventory discussion supplied no numeric Q1 FY2023 consolidated revenue forecast.
January 19 holiday update. The 3.5% net-sales decline measured nine weeks ended December 31, 2022. The revised outlook applied to fiscal 2022.

March 2 Q4 FY2022 release. The forecast decline of 4%–6% applied to full-year FY2023, giving an annual revenue high end of 96% of FY2022. The roughly $400 million Canadian net-sales impact was annual. The $300 million–$350 million Q1 range measured pretax wind-down charges.

March 2 prepared remarks forecast a low-double-digit first-half revenue decline and low-single-digit second-half growth. The first-half forecast combines Q1 and Q2. The roughly 200-basis-point Anniversary Sale shift concerned Q2 and Q3.

Recovered Nordstrom’s full March 2 transcript, including Q&A. The CFO’s 19% Q1 growth figure described the prior year. The 2019 comparisons described halves of FY2022. The quarter-specific breakeven estimate measured EBIT.

Nordstrom dates the call March 2 at 1:45 p.m. Pacific. Its webcast host, https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/tdz9kftu, returned a cache miss. The issuer-hosted transcript above preserved the spoken record.

Exact 3.6 MB deck linked under FY2022 Q4 in Nordstrom’s quarterly archive. The PDF resolved as 23 pages. Text extraction yielded only numerals and bullets. Screenshot attempts returned cache misses or image placeholders without readable slide content, including at https://investor.nordstrom.com/static-files/ab014a62-5edd-4d37-b7e7-063d6df8647b/. The ?download=1 version was inaccessible.
Press-site copy returned 403. The alternate issuer host at https://nordstrom.gcs-web.com/static-files/ab014a62-5edd-4d37-b7e7-063d6df8647b was inaccessible.

The March 2023 archive request was inaccessible. The viewer request at https://docs.google.com/gview?embedded=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Finvestor.nordstrom.com%2Fstatic-files%2Fab014a62-5edd-4d37-b7e7-063d6df8647b also yielded no readable copy.
Checked the remaining March 2 EX-99 exhibit as a possible deck source. It contains the February 28 announcement of a $0.19 quarterly dividend.
April 17 release announced Eric Sprunk’s board appointment and gave no Q1 revenue figure.
May 10 release announced Cathy Smith’s CFO appointment. Its historical double-digit revenue growth reference concerned Target.

May 11 notice scheduled Q1 results for May 31 after market close and supplied no preliminary revenue. Live searches for intervening presentations, conference remarks and trading updates found no qualifying quarter-specific figure.
May 17 announcement, filed May 22, declared a $0.19 dividend and gave no Q1 revenue update.

May 31 actuals, cross-checked against SEC EX-99.1. For the quarters ended April 29, 2023 and April 30, 2022, net sales were $3,064 million and $3,467 million. Net credit card revenues added $117 million and $102 million, giving consolidated totals of $3,181 million and $3,569 million. The headline 11.6% decline measured net sales alone.

The June 7 Form 10-Q confirms the reported perimeter. Canada was deconsolidated March 2, 2023. The current quarter includes Canadian results before that date, and the prior-year quarter includes Canada throughout.
EDGAR records acceptance of the Q1 results 8-K with EX-99.1 on May 31, 2023 at 16:34:56.

publication_date_evidence: Nordstrom’s Q1 release carries a May 31, 2023 Seattle dateline, corroborated by the same-day EDGAR acceptance. The dollar bound is the actual published that day. The unreadable March 2 slides leave the earliest-disclosure date unverified.
